items.followUp: How does cytokinesis take place in an animal cell?

rubric.why: Plant-cell cytokinesis begins with formation of a cell plate at the cell equator.
rubric.description: States that a cell plate forms at the equator of the plant cell.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the cell plate and its location, or for explaining that vesicles form the plate.

rubric.why: The growing cell plate separates the cytoplasm into two daughter cells.
rubric.description: Explains that the cell plate grows outwards and divides the cytoplasm.
rubric.how: Award for describing the plate's outward growth, its joining with the cell boundary, or the resulting division of the cytoplasm.

modelAnswer: In a plant cell, vesicles gather at the equator and fuse to form a cell plate.
The cell plate grows towards the periphery and joins the cell boundary, dividing the cytoplasm into two daughter cells.

items.followUp: What is aneuploidy, and how can it result from an error in cell division?

rubric.why: Non-disjunction occurs when chromosomes or chromatids do not separate properly during cell division.
rubric.description: Defines non-disjunction as failure of chromosome or chromatid separation.
rubric.how: Award for stating that homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids fail to separate.

rubric.why: Failure to separate results in cells or gametes with an abnormal chromosome number.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that cells or gametes may have an abnormal number of chromosomes, including an extra or missing chromosome.

modelAnswer: Non-disjunction is the failure of homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids to separate during cell division.
It produces cells or gametes with an abnormal number of chromosomes; some may have an extra or missing chromosome.

items.followUp: Differentiate between photosynthesis and respiration in terms of energy change.

rubric.why: Anabolism forms complex molecules from simpler ones.
rubric.description: Describes anabolism as building complex molecules from simpler molecules.
rubric.how: Award for stating that anabolism builds or synthesises complex molecules from simpler molecules.

rubric.why: Catabolism breaks complex molecules into simpler ones.
rubric.description: Describes catabolism as breaking complex molecules into simpler molecules.
rubric.how: Award for stating that catabolism breaks down or degrades complex molecules into simpler molecules.

modelAnswer: Anabolism builds complex molecules from simpler molecules and usually requires energy.
Catabolism breaks complex molecules into simpler molecules and usually releases energy.
